name: # The LIVE cross-port divergence ledger -- the AUTHORITATIVE list.
# DIVERGENCE.md at the repository root explains the shape of these
# disagreements and points here; this file is what actually RUNS, so if
# the two ever disagree, this one wins.
# Seven tab-separated columns. `go`, `ts` and `rust` are what each port
# ACTUALLY produces today, as JSON, or ERROR:<code>@<row>:<col>. `opts` is
# a JSON object of make() options, or `-` for a stock parser. Columns are
# read by HEADER NAME in all three runners, so a new runtime column goes
# in without touching the ones already there.
# An error cell pins the POSITION as well as the code, and every runner
# renders one. Two ports can agree on a code and disagree on where they
# say the error happened; a cell that pinned the code alone would sit
# green through exactly that split, and one row here is that split.
# Every row is asserted by EVERY runner: the Go runner must reproduce the
# `go` column, the TS runner the `ts` column and the Rust runner the
# `rust` column, on every run. So a
# divergence that gets FIXED fails this suite as loudly as one that
# regresses, and the row must then be deleted. That is the whole point —
# go/doc/differences.md is prose, and prose rots: through this session it
# claimed 2.e3 and 1e999 still diverged for some time after they were
# aligned, and claimed base-prefixed overflow was aligned before it was.
# A ledger nothing executes is documentation, not a gate.
# Adding a row here is an admission of parity debt, not a way to silence a
# failure. Fix the divergence if you can; record it here only when you
# cannot, with a justification a reader can act on.
string-replace-printable
justification: Control row, not a divergence: printable replacement is aligned. The row that sat above it, string-replace-control (a control character mapped through string.replace, which Go refused as unprintable before consulting the map), was deleted ahead of the engine fix, tabnas/parser#287, so that the fix can land without turning this ledger red; until this repository requires an engine carrying it, Go still refuses that input.

name: string-replace-control-row
justification: A control character mapped through string.replace does not advance the reported row in TypeScript or Go, so the raw \r is reported at 2:6 there. The Rust engine counts the replaced newline as a line and reports 3:1. Only the ROW differs: the code is the same in all three, and the code is the contract. Recorded rather than repaired because the row counting is the engine string lexer, not this grammar.

name: number-sep-space
justification: With a whitespace number separator, the TypeScript number regexp backtracks off the trailing space, which is also an ender, and reads 1 0 as 10. The Go and Rust scanners consume the trailing separator and then decline the whole run. The default separator _ is not an ender in any port, which is why the shared alignment-number-prefix-separator.tsv rows agree everywhere; only a whitespace separator splits. The scanner is the engine lexer, so the repair belongs there.
